newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles plans for revitalized downtown.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles plans for revitalized downtown.

text.p: Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan is preparing a $3 billion plan to revitalise downtown Los Angeles and turn it into a bustling centre for government, work and culture, the Los Angeles Daily News said on Sunday.
The plan will call for large-scale investment in government buildings, cultural centres and urban housing.

The plan, which has been kept a virtual secret outside of downtown business and interest groups, will be revealed to the public in the coming months as planners begin to seek approvals from authorities, the News said.
The proposal would create the second-largest hub of government activity outside of Washington.

The project calls for $265 million in renovations to City Hall, a new federal Immigration and Naturalisation Service building, numerous other government buildings, new parks, urban housing, museums and cultural centres.
The Daily News quoted Riordan, elected in 1993, as saying the plan was needed because downtown was "dysfunctional ... an embarrassment to this city."
Just 25,000 people live in downtown Los Angeles where office vacancies are higher than the national average and many buildings stand empty or derelict, the paper said.
